newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa plans Swiss air cargo rail link.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans Swiss air cargo rail link.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo could launch air cargo feeder services by rail between Germany and Switzerland this autumn, a senior cargo manager said on Thursday.
Hans Driedger, general manager capacity management, said the services would be a joint venture with Swissair and Germany's rail operator, Deutsche Bahn AG (DB).
The three companies had been in talks for over a year to use the newly developed DB Cargo Sprinter as a shuttle container train for airfreight, he explained.
Lufthansa Cargo transported 350,000 tonnes of airfreight by truck between European cities last year.
Driedger said in a Reuters interview: "One idea is to use the DB train for the Frankfurt-Zurich route in cooperation between DB, Lufthansa and Swissair."
"We want to test Zurich and if it is possible, then Munich would be the next destination. It will probably go into service from the autumn," he added.
But a technical solution was still needed since the Cargo Sprinter could only carry a maximum container height of 2.5 metres and not the maximum 3-metre air cargo container height, he noted.

Lufthansa road and rail manager Hartmut Flessa added that the two-year-old five times a week Frankfurt to Milan rail feeder service of Swiss intermodal operator Hupac and German forwarder Mainsped had gone well over the last year.
The airline was also testing sending complete trucks on rail wagons from Frankfurt to Budapest, Venice and Trieste.

Flessa said: "The tests are very successful and we think that we will use rail more. We have a working group with FAG and DB Cargo to evaluate new tracks and procedures for the "rail feeder services".
Deutsche Bahn said last September it was in talks with Lufthansa and Swissair on launching services using the Cargo Sprinter which has been undergoing tests over the last six months.
Swissair cargo manager Germany, Ulf Steinmann, said at the time he planned to switch a large proportion of airfreight from road to rail trucking.
